chapter_title: What is Virginal; or, otherwise, what is Continent?
chapter_note: The chapter is built as a stepped (roughly five-level) definitional sequence: ‘virginal’ vs ‘continent’ mapped to successive cosmic/processual layers of Light (aeons → mixture → purification by the Ambassador → transmigration remainder). The opening Q&A is late hagiographic frame. The middle run (¶3–8) is the strongest core substrate: impersonal cosmological/process language about mixture, purification, ascent, and transmigration. The later paragraphs pivot into institutional/ethical application (elect imagery; sexual renunciation), which reads as pastoral/Christianized extension of the pattern.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic setting and dialogue setup (“the apostle… among the congregation of his church… he says to his disciples”) marks compilation frame, not impersonal cosmological exposition.
Formulaic disciple request (“Proclaim to us, my master…”) is a classic Q&A wrapper around the teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: What is called ‘virginal’ is assigned to the mystery of the aeons of greatness. And they called it ‘virginal’ by the category of all the light that did not [taste] of death, nor come to the enemy’s war.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution / frame formula: “Then speaks our enlightener to them:”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is the aeons-of-greatness definition and the light/death/war criterion (cosmic-process description). The removed lead-in is a late instructional frame marker.

paragraphs.core_text: However, what is called ‘continent’ occurs to the mystery of the light that came and was mixed with the darkness. It was defiled in bodies [ ... ] and went up to the light. [They] called [it ‘co]ntinent’.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological/process mapping (Light → mixture with Darkness → defilement in bodies → ascent) stays within the system; no institutional address or citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, the holy vir[gin]als [ ... ... ] should they come out against the en[emy ... ... not] taste death, nor [ ... ].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary but continues the same cosmological criterion (“not taste death… against the enemy”) without audience exhortation or church-institution identifiers.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.249⟩ On the other hand, what is called ‘continent’ [is this li]ght that mixed with the darkness, was purif[ie]d, came [up f]rom all the creatures, and was confirmed in the great[ness]. They called it ‘continent’ since it tasted [of the l]ust; but afterwards was cleansed from it and [become an] holy one.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal mechanics of mixture/purification/ascent; “lust” functions as a state of contamination within the cosmic process, not a direct moral injunction.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, what is called [‘vi]rginal’ is this light that was purified by the ima[ge] of the [A]mbassador. It wen[t up and] attained [the] he[ights. It was] confirmed in the image of the gods.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic core cosmology: purification by the (Third) Ambassador’s image, ascent, confirmation among gods—no institutional referents.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, what is [called] ‘continent’ is the remainder of this light th[at] remained behind, from what was cleansed. It goes up and comes down in transmigration. Al[so], there is a part [of] it that shall come and attain the form of [hum]an [fl]esh. Again, that one too shall be chosen in the flesh, [accept] the hope, and become an holy one. And they name it ‘continent’.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Processual teaching on the ‘remainder’ and transmigration (up/down movement; eventual human flesh) is substrate-like. The phrasing “[accept] the hope” slightly gestures toward later soteriological idiom, but it remains embedded in the cosmic mechanism rather than exhortation or NT citation.

Pattern is extended into institutional/para-Christian anthropology: “images of the elect” (church category) and “new man/old man” (strong Pauline idiom) apply the schema to community/personhood rather than staying cosmos→cosmos.
Explicit ethical/sexual definitions “in the flesh” (virginity vs renunciation after having a woman) are institutional moral application, not cosmological mechanism.
Concluding pedagogical summary (“Behold, I have taught you…”) functions as editorial closure/lesson-capping rather than core exposition.
